intro: B2: mass tourism, «slow» travel, a complaint to a travel agency, rail vs air. We practise argumentation on a topic where everyone has their own experience.
speaking.0.promptUa: Describe the illustration and comment on the phenomenon of mass tourism. Say what benefits and problems it brings for residents and suggest how to travel responsibly.
speaking.0.phrases.0.ua: In the foreground you can see…, and in the background…
speaking.0.phrases.1.ua: Mass tourism has both advantages and disadvantages.
speaking.0.phrases.3.ua: It's worth choosing less popular places.
speaking.0.tips.0: **Zarówno…, jak i…** («both…and…») — a complex B2 conjunction that adds precision.
speaking.0.tips.1: Justify: **not «turystyka jest zła»**, but «ma zalety i wady» — the examiner values balance.
speaking.0.tips.2: A specific piece of advice at the end («wybierać poza sezonem») is stronger than the general «trzeba dbać o środowisko».
speaking.1.promptUa: Do travels really teach more than school? State your opinion, give examples and take opponents' arguments into account.
speaking.1.phrases.0.ua: I believe that travel teaches many things, but…
speaking.1.phrases.1.ua: Contact with another culture helps get rid of stereotypes.
speaking.1.phrases.3.ua: To sum up, travel broadens horizons, but…
speaking.1.tips.0: A personal story («kiedy zamieszkałam w Polsce…») is the best argument and easier to remember.
speaking.1.tips.1: **Nie da się znaleźć w podręcznikach** — the impersonal «da się» («it is possible») — a B2 construction.
speaking.1.tips.2: The final «ale wartościowe stają się dopiero wtedy, gdy…» — a nuanced conclusion instead of a categorical one.
speaking.2.promptUa: You have returned from a trip organised by a travel agency, but the hotel didn't match the offer. You are talking to an agency employee. State the problem, answer his questions and outline your expectations.
speaking.2.phrases.0.ua: I would like to make a complaint because…
speaking.2.phrases.1.ua: It turned out that… doesn't match the description in the offer.
speaking.2.phrases.2.ua: I have e-mail confirmation and photos.
speaking.2.phrases.3.ua: I expect a refund of part of the costs.
speaking.2.tips.0: Order of arguments: **what was promised → what it was really like → what you did → what you expect**.
speaking.2.tips.1: Specifics («okna na parking», «klimatyzacja») convince better than «było źle».
speaking.2.tips.2: **Rzecznik konsumentów** — the consumer ombudsman: mentioning them is a mild but serious argument.
writing.0.promptUa: You are organising a company trip. Because of the weather forecast you have to change the programme. Write an e-mail to participants: announce the change, give the new plan for the day, ask for suitable clothing and for confirmation of attendance by the end of the week.
writing.0.phrases.0.ua: In view of the weather forecast…
writing.0.phrases.2.ua: Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes.
writing.0.tips.0: **Ze względu na + accusative** («in view of») — more formal than «z powodu», good for a business e-mail.
writing.0.tips.1: Separate the information: **what changed / what stays / what's needed from participants** — the reader finds everything fast.
writing.1.promptUa: A discussion is under way in the city about limiting short domestic flights in favour of rail. Write a letter to the editor of a local newspaper stating your position. Take into account ecological and practical arguments, refer to your own travel experience and propose a specific solution.
writing.1.phrases.0.ua: In connection with the ongoing discussion I would like to state my position.
writing.1.phrases.2.ua: However, I understand the opponents' concerns.
writing.1.phrases.3.ua: Therefore I propose introducing restrictions gradually.
writing.1.tips.0: A letter to the editor: **occasion → position → arguments → opponents → proposal**. A formal register without aggression.
writing.1.tips.1: **Pod warunkiem, że…** in the thesis immediately shows an honest position: «yes, but on condition that…».
writing.1.tips.2: Acknowledging opponents' arguments («trzeba to uczciwie przyznać») increases trust in the text.
listening.0.intro: An interview with a travel blogger.
grammar.0.intro: Conditional sentences, relative pronouns, consequence constructions.
grammar.0.questions.1.why: **których pociąg** — «whose train»: the possessive form in the plural: «podróżni, których pociąg…».
grammar.0.questions.3.why: An unreal condition in the past → **tryb warunkowy** in the main clause: «zdążylibyśmy».
grammar.0.questions.4.why: **jeśli + future** — a condition: «jeśli nie potwierdzą, zostanie anulowana».
